default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1458.title: Efficiency-ratio trend ignition
E-1458.hypothesis: When price covers a window almost in a straight line (net move close to the sum of bar moves) a directional parent order is being worked without pushback; follow the first bar the ratio gets high.

E-1459.title: Confirmed swing-point break
E-1459.hypothesis: A close through the latest confirmed fractal swing high/low (fresh enough) takes out the stops sitting behind the swing; follow it.

E-1460.title: Single-bar jump dominance fade
E-1460.hypothesis: When one bar is the largest in the window and makes up a big share of all movement, it is a liquidity gap/stop burst rather than a trend; the next side to trade is the liquidity provider, so fade it.

E-1461.title: New extreme on opposing signed volume
E-1461.hypothesis: A new window high made while the colour-signed volume of the window is net selling (low: net buying) shows the extreme was reached by passive fills, not initiative; fade it.

E-1462.title: Stale session-extreme break
E-1462.hypothesis: A session high/low untouched for a long time accumulates resting stops and breakout orders; a close through it after the stale period releases them in that direction.

E-1463.title: Big-bar midpoint hold
E-1463.hypothesis: After an unusually large bar, a pullback into its midpoint that closes back beyond it in the bar's direction shows the aggressors keep control of the half-way level; follow.

E-1464.title: Prior-session VWAP line cross
E-1464.hypothesis: Yesterday's VWAP is the average price of the previous session's participants; the first close beyond it shifts who is in profit across sessions; follow the cross.

E-1465.title: Marubozu window breakout
E-1465.hypothesis: A bar that closes at its extreme and takes the window's high/low leaves no counter-trading inside the bar: aggressors paid every price; follow it.

E-1466.title: Second-entry pullback in an EMA trend
E-1466.hypothesis: In a trend (price on one side of the EMA) a pullback with at least two counter-trend bar extremes, ended by a bar closing through the prior bar, is the second attempt that shakes out weak hands; trade with the trend.

E-1467.title: Heavy-day VWAP side change
E-1467.hypothesis: When the session's cumulative volume runs well above its usual pace, VWAP is a heavily defended benchmark; a close across it flips the benchmarked algos' side; follow the cross.
